newsitem.title: UK: Mideast crude tanker rates firm, upside potential.
newsitem.headline: Mideast crude tanker rates firm, upside potential.

text.p: Crude tanker chartering got off to a slow start on Monday but freight rates in the key Middle East Gulf remained buoyant. Other sectors were also seeing last week's firmer rates holding and in some cases being built upon.

VLCC trips to Japan broke through W90 last week to reach highs not seen since the Gulf War seven years ago. Shipping brokers said they saw no immediate factor to indicate rates would start to ease back.
"Tonnage is tight right into September and shipowners have got used to asking for high rates and getting them," said one.
VLCCs to Japan are pegged around W92.5-95 with Singapore around W83-85 and trips West about W10-15 lower.
With demand in Asia strong and suitable ships in short supply rates could edge up further, shippers said.

In the West African market Suezmaxes were attracting a little under W100 for trips to the U.S. with the real chance of W100 being breached. Shipbrokers said million barrel vessels were becoming difficult to find and that double stemming in VLCCs was likely to increase.
The tightening of the West African market has been a result of increased Med activity because of Iraqi exports from Ceyhan.

In the Mediterranean, Black Sea theatre 130,000 tonners were attracting up to W95. Aframaxes in the Med have not been left out of the rally in rates and 80,000 tonners were getting fixed at a little under W110 for cross Med trips.
In the UK/continent market activity has slowed a little after a flurry of fixtures bumped rates up to W135 for inter-UKC trips on 80,000 tonners.
The Caribs up U.S. coast market has shown strong business with rates tracking higher in the mid to high W140s for 70,000 tonners.
